# Juniper Pros / Fun Facts
- Junos OS has the ability to roll back to previous configurations. This feature allows administrators to revert to an earlier configuration state, which is invaluable for quickly recovering from configuration errors or undesired changes. Junos OS maintains an archive of previous configurations, enabling easy rollback to any saved state. 
- Configuration Files
	> - active
		- active configuration is what’s currently running on the device
	> - candidate configuration is what has been modified and not committed to the device
	> -  View the configuration file
		- Hierarchy view 
			- `show configuration`
		- Set View (looks like Cisco)
			-  `show configuration | display set`
  
- Another significant advantage of Junos OS is its modular design. The operating system is structured so that different processes and services run in separate protected memory spaces, enhancing the stability and reliability of the system. If one process fails, it does not affect the others, thereby minimizing the risk of system-wide failures.

- The <mark style="background: #ADCCFFA6;">configure private</mark> command each user gets their own candidate configuration
	> - When multiple users are configuring a Junos device using the "configure private" command, each user gets their own candidate configuration (C). This allows for isolated configuration sessions, where changes made by one user do not impact or interfere with the changes made by another user in their private session.
	  

- Junos OS can store up to 50 rollback configuration files. These rollback files allow administrators to revert to previous configurations, providing a safety net that facilitates recovery from configuration errors or undesired changes

- Link State Routing Protocols
	- Are a type of routing protocol used in packet- switching networks for finding the best path between source and destination. <mark style="background: #ADCCFFA6;">OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) and IS-IS (Intermediate System to Intermediate System) are both examples of link-state routing protocols</mark>. They work by maintaining a complete map or topology of the network, allowing routers to independently calculate the best path to each destination. Unlike distance-vector protocols like RIP, link-state protocols are more efficient and scalable, making them suitable for larger networks.

- The <mark style="background: #ADCCFFA6;">help apropos</mark> command displays the context that references a specified variable 
	> - This command is used in the configuration prompt and example is "help apropos archive"




# Juniper Network Interfaces
## Interface Naming and Logical Units
- xe, et, ge, mge - indicates the physical interface presentation

| Interface Type | Interface capability         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- |
| fe             | Fast Eithernet (100)         |
| ge             | Gigabit Ethernet (1Gbps)     |
| mge            | Gigabit Ethernet (1Gbps)     |
| xe             | 10 Gbps Ethernet             |
| et             | Ethernet (40 Gbps and above) |
- 0/0/3 - indicates the location on the chassis
- FPC
	- Flexible PIC Concentrator
		- Junipers technical name for the actual line card itself
- PIC
	- Physical Interface Card
		- The interface card within a line card, OR a specific section of a bigger line card
- xe-<mark style="background: #BBFABBA6;">4</mark>/<mark style="background: #ABF7F7A6;">2</mark>/<mark style="background: #ADCCFFA6;">0</mark>
	- <mark style="background: #BBFABBA6;">FPC</mark>
	- <mark style="background: #ABF7F7A6;">PIC</mark>
	- <mark style="background: #ADCCFFA6;">Port</mark>
